title: Probe storm amplification caused circuit-breaker cascades and asymmetric SLO misses
creator: Marco Li
description: Summary: On 2026-03-02 we observed an unexpected cascade of circuit-breaker trips in our eu-west-1 region that propagated to us-east-1 via probe-driven fanout. The event resulted in a sustained SLO miss for generation tail latency (p95/p99) for 18 minutes and intermittent 5xx error spikes for a subset of enterprise tenants. Root cause was a combination of a probe retry storm, misrouted health-check traffic hitting production model replicas, and a circuit hysteresis configuration that amplified partial degradations into regional failovers. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations performed, and a set of prioritized action items.
timeline: 2026-03-02T09:42Z: Elevated 5xx alerts from eu-west-1 model pool reported by telemetry (first spike)
2026-03-02T09:43Z: Automated routing attempted local mitigation - small fraction of traffic re-routed to secondary pool in same region
2026-03-02T09:44Z: Health-check probes from deploy-sanity job spiked after a partial cache warmup failure; probe retry multiplier set to 3 sent bursts every 5s
2026-03-02T09:45Z: Circuit breakers for several clusters entered Open state due to increased error-rate + elevated latency; control plane started cascading fallback policies
2026-03-02T09:46Z: Smart routing initiated cross-region rebalances to us-east-1 and ap-south-1, increasing load on secondary regions
2026-03-02T09:50Z: Secondary regions experienced queueing and KV-cache cold-starts; additional circuits tripped in an asymmetric pattern
2026-03-02T10:00Z: On-call (Aisha) paged; manual soft-fallback to compatible quantized model variants enabled for impacted tenants
2026-03-02T10:20Z: Traffic shaping and rate-limits applied; probe retry configuration rolled back to baseline for deploy-sanity job
2026-03-02T10:30Z: P95/P99 latency SLO returned to normal for most tenants; incident declared resolved at 10:48Z after monitoring held stable
root_cause: A coordinated sequence: a transient KV-cache warmup regression in eu-west-1 triggered a deploy-sanity probe job to rapidly retry health checks. Those probes were misrouted at the proxy layer to production inference replicas (misconfiguration in probe-target mapping). The probe retry bursts produced an elevated error-rate and latency which pushed several circuit-breakers into Open with hysteresis parameters that favored aggressive failover. Smart routing then redistributed traffic to secondary regions, creating new cold-starts and queueing, amplifying the initial load and causing further circuit trips — a positive feedback loop.
contributing_factors: probe-target mapping misconfiguration: deploy-sanity job probe endpoint overlapped with production replica endpoint during recent routing change
probe retry multiplier too aggressive (set to 3) for multi-region health checks
circuit-breaker hysteresis periods and backoff were tuned for availability but not for probe-amplified transient errors
lack of a probe tag/labelging system to distinguish synthetic traffic from customer requests at the edge router
KV-cache warmup regression introduced by recent runtime patch (kernel selection path) increased tail latency for cold requests
mitigations_taken: rolled back deploy-sanity probe routing change and isolated probe traffic to a non-production probe pool
temporarily lowered probe retry multiplier to 0 for the failing job and added exponential backoff to probe logic
manually adjusted circuit-breaker hysteresis windows to prevent immediate cross-region failover during high probe churn
enabled soft-fallback to quantized-compatible model variants for impacted customers to reduce latency and 5xx errors
applied a hotfix to the KV-cache warmup path to reduce cold-start tail latency (canary deployed)
long_term_actions: Implement probe tagging and edge-level filtering: require a mandatory 'x-probe: true' header for synthetic health checks and ensure routers drop those from production replica pools
Add a probe-runbook and CI guardrail that prevents probe endpoint overlap with production inference endpoints (deploy-time validation)
Rework circuit-breaker configuration: introduce probe-awareness and a graded hysteresis policy that treats synthetic-error bursts differently from user-error bursts
Improve KV-cache warmup: add proactive pre-warm based on predicted traffic and model-version pinning during rollouts
Add a canary for routing changes that runs isolated probes and verifies correct probe-target mapping before global rollout
Create a cross-region capacity safety buffer during automated smart-routing to avoid immediate overload of secondary regions
Enhance observability: add a dashboard that correlates probe volume, probe error-rate, circuit state transitions, and cross-region traffic shifts
postmortem_notes: Impact: 18 minutes of elevated p99 for a subset of enterprise tenants; several tenants experienced transient 5xx and degraded throughput — we estimate potential revenue impact for directly impacted calls only
Detection: alerting threshold was triggered by elevated 5xx rates; correlation with probe traffic was not immediate and required manual investigation of edge logs
Communication: status pages and customer notifications were sent within 25 minutes; post-incident emails to affected enterprise customers are drafted
Lessons learned: synthetic traffic must never be allowed to generate production-level load; circuit configs need to be robust to synthetic bursts; routing changes require stricter deploy-time checks
